sheets.rejected_alternative: A CLAUDE.md rule saying 'never deploy unless the user asks'. That is a request the model interprets, not a gate; the whole point of the requirement is that it must hold even when the model's own reasoning concludes the code is ready.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness for the trigger: with disable-model-invocation set, Claude Code does not put the skill in Claude's context and does not let the model load it, so the invocation gate does not depend on model restraint. The model still owns execution quality once a human types the command.
sheets.context_boundary: Main session context, and nothing at all until the human types the command: the description is withheld, so the skill has zero context cost while unused. On invocation the rendered body enters as one message and stays for the session. With context: fork the procedure runs in a subagent's own window and only its result returns.
sheets.lifecycle: Starts only on the explicit /deploy invocation (and, from v2.1.196, is likewise blocked from firing when a scheduled task names the skill as its prompt). The allowed-tools grant covers just that turn and clears at your next message; the instructions themselves persist in context for the session.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the skill, but open for the underlying capability: the flag stops Claude from invoking the deploy skill, not from running the deploy commands directly if it decides to. If the guarantee has to be absolute, back it with a permission deny rule (or a PreToolUse hook) on the deploy command itself and let the skill be the human-triggered path through that gate. The secondary cost is that Claude cannot suggest the skill either, since it is invisible until invoked.
sheets.version_caveat: No plan restriction. disable-model-invocation defaults to false, so the gate exists only if you set it; from v2.1.218 it accepts yes/on/1 as well as true. Its coverage of scheduled tasks requires v2.1.196 or later, and it also prevents the skill from being preloaded into subagents. The background: false option for a forked skill requires v2.1.218.

scenarios.scenario: Our repo contains .env files and a secrets/ directory holding live credentials. The agent must never be able to read those paths with its built-in tools, and the restriction should be checked into the repo so every teammate gets it automatically.

key.primary: permissions.deny rules such as Read(./.env), Read(./.env.*), and Read(./secrets/**) in the project's .claude/settings.json
key.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook script that inspects file paths and blocks reads of the secret locations
key.rejection_reason: A custom hook reimplements what declarative deny rules already provide and misses coverage the rules get for free: Read deny rules also apply to @file mentions, Grep and Glob, IDE-shared context, and recognized Bash file commands like cat, head, tail, and sed. The settings docs' own secrets example uses permissions.deny, deny rules merge from every scope, and no allow rule or hook allow decision can override them.
key.context_boundary: no context window (deny rules are evaluated by Claude Code at the tool-call boundary, not by the model); what the boundary guarantees is that matching secret file contents never cross into context, with coverage extending beyond the Read tool to Grep, Glob, @file mentions, and IDE-shared context
key.lifecycle: evaluated by the permission system before every tool call; deny rules are checked before ask and allow, and deny/ask rules in project settings apply without workspace trust
key.failure_mode: Deny rules bind the built-in tools and recognized Bash file commands only; an arbitrary subprocess such as a Python script calling open() can still read the file, which only OS-level sandboxing prevents.
key.version_caveat: none for the core behavior; a Read deny rule additionally blocking the Edit tool on the same path requires v2.1.208 or later

sheets.primary: Permission deny rules in the repo's checked-in .claude/settings.json, expressed as path-scoped denials for the file-reading tools (a deny entry covering Read on ./.env and ./secrets/**, plus the same paths for the edit tools), so the restriction travels with the clone.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook that inspects the requested path and blocks it; more code, more ways to get the path normalization wrong, and it duplicates a permission layer the harness already has.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Permission rules are evaluated by Claude Code before the tool runs, and deny takes precedence over any allow rule, so the model cannot talk its way past them.
sheets.context_boundary: Rule evaluation happens entirely in the harness process at tool-call time; nothing about the file contents ever enters the model's context, only a refusal message naming the denied path.
sheets.lifecycle: Loaded at session start from the project settings file whenever the agent runs with that repo as its working directory, and applies for the whole session; it lapses if someone edits the file, if the agent is run from a different cwd, or if a user-level or managed setting reshapes the permission set.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built-in file tools, but it is a tool-level block, not a filesystem block: a Bash call such as cat .env, a grep, or a Python script the agent writes reads the same bytes unless matching Bash deny rules exist too. Path matching is also literal, so a symlink or an absolute path spelled differently can slip past a rule written only in relative form.
sheets.version_caveat: The permission-rule syntax for path arguments (the Read(...) style specifier and the gitignore-flavoured globs) has changed across Claude Code releases, and earlier versions did not support path scoping on read at all; I cannot state the exact minimum version from memory, so the rules must be smoke-tested on the team's installed version before being trusted.

sheets.primary: Permission deny rules checked into the repo's .claude/settings.json: Read(.env), Read(**/.env) and Read(secrets/**), each paired with the matching Edit(...) deny rule. The rules travel with the clone, so every teammate inherits them with no per machine setup.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook on Read that exits 2 for those paths. It would also be checked in, but it is more code for the same outcome and it never fires for files pulled in by an @ reference in a prompt, where the docs direct you to a Read deny rule instead.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Permission rules are evaluated by Claude Code before the tool runs, so prompt text or CLAUDE.md wording cannot change what is allowed.
sheets.context_boundary: The check happens in the harness before any file content is produced, so the credential never enters the model's context window; only the denial message crosses to the model.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated on every matching tool call in every session started in that repo, in effect from the moment the repo is cloned because deny and ask rules apply without the workspace trust dialog. It stops applying only if the rules are deleted.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built in file tools and for the file commands Claude Code recognizes inside Bash, such as cat, head and sed, but it is not a filesystem boundary: a Python or Node script the agent launches opens the same paths freely. Symlinks are covered, since a deny rule matches either the link or its target.
sheets.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path only from v2.1.208. Write, NotebookEdit and Glob path rules are accepted but never consulted (v2.1.210 warns at startup), so write Edit(...) and Read(...) rules and nothing else.

sheets.primary: permissions.deny rules committed in the repository's .claude/settings.json: Read(./.env), Read(./.env.*), Read(**/.env) and Read(./secrets/**), with matching Edit(...) deny entries for the same paths. Deny rules are evaluated before ask and allow, are not gated by the workspace trust dialog (only allow rules and additionalDirectories are), and cannot be re-opened by any user-level setting or CLI flag, so every teammate inherits them on clone.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook that inspects tool_input.file_path and exits 2 on a match. It has the same subprocess blind spot, adds a script to maintain, and can be switched off with disableAllHooks, so it buys nothing over a deny rule here.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code itself, not by the model; prompt or CLAUDE.md text shapes what Claude attempts but never changes what is allowed.
sheets.context_boundary: Evaluated inside the CLI process before the tool executes, so nothing about the secret ever enters the model's context window; Claude only sees a denial message. A path-scoped rule leaves the Read tool available and blocks only the matching calls, unlike a bare-name deny which would strip the tool from Claude's context entirely.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies from session start to every Read, Grep, Glob, @-file mention and IDE-shared selection, plus file-reading Bash commands Claude Code recognizes. It applies for as long as the file is present in the repo and can only be lifted by editing the committed file, which is a reviewable change.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built-in file tools and for recognized Bash file commands such as cat, head, tail and sed, but fails open for arbitrary subprocesses: a Python or Node script that opens the path itself is not covered. The other common trap is path anchoring, where a single leading slash anchors at the settings source rather than the filesystem root, so a rule silently matches nothing.
sheets.version_caveat: From v2.1.208 a Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path, but Write and NotebookEdit are still not covered, so explicit Edit(...) deny rules are required. From v2.1.210 Claude Code warns at startup that path rules written for Write, NotebookEdit or Glob are accepted but never consulted. For enforcement that also stops spawned processes you need sandbox filesystem settings, which are macOS, Linux and WSL2 only.

sheets.primary: permissions.deny rules committed in the repository's .claude/settings.json: Read(.env) and Read(secrets/**), plus matching Edit(.env) and Edit(secrets/**) rules so no file-editing tool can create or rewrite those paths either. Checking the file into git is what makes every teammate inherit it on clone.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook matching Read that exits 2 on those paths. It loses because it is an executable script each teammate must have working, it can fail open on a bad interpreter or missing jq, and hook decisions are evaluated after deny rules anyway, so the rule is both simpler and strictly more authoritative.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. The permission layer evaluates the rule before the tool call is dispatched, independently of anything the prompt or CLAUDE.md says.
sheets.context_boundary: Evaluated entirely inside Claude Code before any tool runs, so no byte of the denied file enters the model's context window. The rule is also applied best-effort to Grep, Glob, @file mentions in prompts, and IDE-shared open-file context.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies to every matching tool call for the whole session, in the main agent and in subagents, and it takes effect without the workspace trust dialog because deny rules only restrict. It stops applying only if someone edits the rule out of the committed settings file.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for built-in file tools and for the file-reading Bash commands Claude Code recognizes such as cat, head, tail, and sed, but fails open for arbitrary subprocesses: a Python or Node script the agent launches opens .env directly and the rule never sees it. Path rules written against Write, NotebookEdit, or Glob are accepted but never consulted.
sheets.version_caveat: A Read deny rule extends to the Edit tool on the same path only from Claude Code v2.1.208; Write and NotebookEdit are still not covered, so pair every Read deny with an Edit deny. From v2.1.210 a path rule on Write or Glob is ignored with a startup warning.

scenarios.scenario: The platform team must guarantee that the only automation scripts, on-demand instruction packages, custom agent definitions, and external tool servers that ever load are the ones IT ships centrally. Nothing a developer adds on their own machine or commits into a repo may take effect.

key.primary: strictPluginOnlyCustomization in managed settings, which locks skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers to plugin or managed sources; paired with strictKnownMarketplaces and disableSideloadFlags to control the plugin channel itself
key.rejection_reason: allowManagedHooksOnly blocks only user, project, and non-force-enabled plugin hooks; skills, custom agents, and MCP servers from user and project sources still load. strictPluginOnlyCustomization is the managed-only key documented to lock all four customization surfaces (or a named subset such as ["skills", "hooks"]) so they can come only from plugins or managed settings.
key.context_boundary: no context window (a load-time gate the harness reads from managed settings); skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources are blocked from loading at all, so nothing from those sources ever reaches any session or its context
key.lifecycle: read from managed settings at startup; blocks loading of skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources for the whole session
key.failure_mode: Leaves bypass channels open unless companions are set: the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config CLI flags still work without disableSideloadFlags, and marketplace sources stay open without strictKnownMarketplaces; it also blocks developers' legitimate personal tooling, forcing everything through plugin packaging.
key.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires v2.1.193 or later; no version gate is documented for strictPluginOnlyCustomization itself

sheets.primary: Managed settings with strictPluginOnlyCustomization set to true, with IT shipping the approved hooks, skills, subagents, and MCP servers as plugins from a company marketplace, locked down with strictKnownMarketplaces and disableSideloadFlags. The one key names all four surfaces the requirement lists.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Assembling the per-surface managed locks by hand, namely allowManagedHooksOnly plus allowManagedMcpServersOnly plus Agent(...) deny rules. It covers hooks and MCP servers but leaves skills in ~/.claude/skills and .claude/skills and agent definitions in the matching agents directories still loading, so the guarantee has holes the single setting closes.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code skips the user-level and project-level source directories at load time, so the blocked material is never registered and the model never learns it existed.
sheets.context_boundary: This is a load-time decision made before any conversation context is assembled. Blocked skills never enter the skill index and blocked agents never enter the agent registry, so none of their descriptions or bodies occupy the model's context window.
sheets.lifecycle: Applied at startup for every session on a machine that receives the managed policy, and re-evaluated when configuration reloads. It stops applying only when IT removes the policy, and it never blocks built-in agents, bundled skills, or anything in the managed policy directory.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the four named surfaces, but the guarantee is only as strong as the supply chain around it: without strictKnownMarketplaces a developer installs an approved-looking plugin from their own marketplace, and without disableSideloadFlags they bypass the marketplace allowlist for a single run with --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, or --mcp-config. Slash commands and output styles are outside the four locked surfaces.
sheets.version_caveat: strictPluginOnlyCustomization is managed-settings only, with no effect from user or project files, and disableSideloadFlags requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later. Surface names an older client does not recognize are ignored rather than rejected, so version skew across the fleet degrades enforcement quietly instead of failing loudly.

sheets.primary: Ship the approved automation as a single IT-owned plugin (hooks, skills, subagents and MCP server definitions bundled together) from a marketplace the platform team controls, and pin it through the managed enterprise settings file distributed by MDM, using the managed layer to fix which MCP servers and extension sources may load rather than leaving discovery to project and user directories.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Committing the same set into each repo's .claude/ directory, which distributes the content but grants no exclusivity: anything else a developer adds locally or in the repo loads alongside it.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness, via the managed settings precedence, and only to the extent the version exposes switches for each extension source; anything not covered by a switch falls back to being a machine-image and code-review control rather than an enforced one.
sheets.context_boundary: Resolution happens at session startup in the harness. Only the resulting definitions reach the model context, and skills in particular enter lazily, with names and descriptions loaded up front and bodies pulled in on demand, so the central bundle should be sized with that in mind.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated when a session starts (and again when configuration is reloaded), applying to every session on the managed machine until MDM changes the policy or the plugin version is rolled forward.
sheets.failure_mode: The honest risk is incomplete coverage: settings precedence reliably stops a developer from overriding a managed value, but that is not the same as preventing an additional locally defined skill, subagent or project MCP server from being discovered, and a developer with local admin can edit the managed file. Where a source has no disable switch, the control is advisory and fails open silently, with no signal that an extra extension loaded.
sheets.version_caveat: Plugins, plugin marketplaces and the managed-settings keys that gate MCP servers and other extension sources are relatively recent and have moved between releases; I cannot confirm from memory that a single switch exists today to disable project-level and user-level skill and subagent discovery. That specific claim must be checked against the installed version's settings reference before compliance sign-off, and a fleet minimum version pinned.

sheets.primary: Managed settings carrying strictPluginOnlyCustomization true, so hooks, skills, agents and MCP servers load only from plugins or the managed policy, combined with strictKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins to pin the vetted plugin supply and disableSideloadFlags to close the CLI bypass.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Checked in project .claude/ configuration. Rejected because it can distribute IT's components but has no power to suppress what a developer adds in their own home directory or commits into a repo they control.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code skips the user level and project level sources for each locked surface while it assembles the session, so nothing is left to the model or to developer discipline.
sheets.context_boundary: Applied before the first model call, while the CLI loads configuration, so a blocked skill, agent, hook or server never enters the context window at all. The developer sees only that their local component did not load.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated at startup for every session on the machine, surface by surface, and in force until IT changes the managed policy. Unlocked surfaces keep loading from user and project sources as usual.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed for the four named surfaces, but the guarantee leaks through the plugin channel: without strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces a developer can still install a plugin from a marketplace they control, and without disableSideloadFlags they can bypass the marketplace allowlist for a single run with --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents or --mcp-config.
sheets.version_caveat: disableSideloadFlags requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later, so on older clients those CLI flags remain an open bypass and the lock is only as strong as the fleet's minimum version. Surface names the client does not recognise are ignored rather than rejected, so a typo in the array silently locks nothing.

sheets.primary: Managed settings with strictPluginOnlyCustomization set to true, which locks all four named surfaces at once: hooks (the automation scripts), skills (the on-demand instruction packages), agents (the custom agent definitions) and mcp (the external tool servers). Combine it with strictKnownMarketplaces to pin where plugins may come from, enabledPlugins in the same managed source to force-enable the vetted plugins, and disableSideloadFlags to reject --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config.
sheets.rejected_alternative: allowManagedHooksOnly together with allowManagedMcpServersOnly. Those two locks are real but cover only hooks and MCP servers, leaving ~/.claude/skills, .claude/skills, ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents loading normally, which is half the stated requirement.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness. For each locked surface the loader skips user-level and project-level sources entirely and loads only plugin-provided and managed-policy sources, and managed settings cannot be overridden by any other scope including command line arguments.
sheets.context_boundary: This is a load-time decision inside the CLI process. Its effect on context is that a blocked skill, agent or MCP tool never appears to the model in the first place, so there is nothing to invoke and no instruction to ignore: the surface is absent rather than forbidden.
sheets.lifecycle: Evaluated at startup and again on each settings reload, for every session on a managed device. Blocked marketplace sources are checked before any network request, so they never touch the filesystem, and the restriction re-applies on plugin install, update, refresh and auto-update. It stops applying if the device leaves management.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on a managed device and fails open off it: an unenrolled machine, a container image, or an older CLI build has no policy to enforce. Two quieter gaps: unrecognized surface names in the array are ignored rather than rejected, so a typo silently leaves a surface unlocked, and CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules and slash commands are not among the four locked surfaces, so instruction-shaped customization still flows in from repos.
sheets.version_caveat: strictPluginOnlyCustomization and strictKnownMarketplaces are managed-settings-only and have no effect in user or project settings; disableSideloadFlags requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later. Managed settings parse tolerantly, so an entry that fails validation is stripped with a warning while the rest of the policy stays enforced, which means a broken lock can go unnoticed: validate with claude doctor on a test machine before a fleet rollout.
